I'm also working through the indexing convention for the distance and path matrices, confirming how idx2(i,j,n) maps row/column pairs into the flattened array.\n\nFor Floyd-Warshall, I'm reasoning that the in-place update is safe since modifying row/column k during iteration k doesn't actually change their values, meaning the i,j ordering doesn't matter and parallelizing across rows with OpenMP produces identical results to the sequential version—only the loop over k needs to stay sequential. I'm also noting there's no INF handling needed since distances stay bounded, and I need to preserve the original unsigned integer overflow semantics exactly.\n\nNow I'm thinking through the MPI row-block distribution strategy, where each iteration k requires broadcasting row k and gathering the local column k values from each process's owned rows.\n\nSince dist rows are contiguous by row-major storage, I can gather both matrices to rank 0 with MPI_Gatherv after timing ends, so it doesn't affect the measured computation cost. The spec requires unconditional use of the specified approach, so the CUDA path must always run, even without checking for a fallback.\n\nFor OpenMP's role, I'm thinking it fits best on the host side: multi-GPU dispatch per node, data initialization, and validation work, rather than altering the core numerical kernel. The tricky part is that matrix initialization relies on a sequential rand_r stream, so parallelizing it with OpenMP threads would break determinism unless I carefully skip-ahead the random sequence per thread.\n\nA real hybrid approach: MPI across nodes, OpenMP threads each owning a GPU within a node, and CUDA kernels doing the per-GPU work—so each k iteration requires broadcasting row k from its owning GPU to the others.\n\nThe synchronous D2H copy naturally waits on prior kernel completion since it's on the same stream, so ordering works out fine. For MPI thread safety, only the master thread should call MPI_Bcast, so I'll need MPI_Init_thread with at least FUNNELED support. This is getting complex, so I'm weighing whether a simpler one-GPU-per-rank design with OpenMP just for host-side init might be more practical than full multi-GPU-per-node support.\n\nI'll settle on: each MPI rank owns a contiguous row block, and within that rank, OpenMP threads bind round-robin to visible GPUs, with thread count equal to min(device count, local rows). This handles both the common launcher setup where CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES gives one GPU per rank, and the case where a single rank sees multiple devices on a node. Device sharing across ranks via modulo assignment should also work fine without causing issues.\n\nNow I'm working through the pipelined update for row k: the thread owning k's sub-block copies the row device-to-host, an OpenMP barrier synchronizes, the row is broadcast via MPI, another barrier follows, and then each thread copies the row back to its device and launches a kernel to relax distances in its assigned sub-block using the broadcast row.\n\nI realize there's a race condition between iterations: without a barrier after the host-to-device copy step, the owner thread for the next row could overwrite the shared host buffer while another thread is still reading it for the current iteration. The fix is to double-buffer the host row (alternating by k's parity) so writes for k+1 don't collide with reads still in flight for k.\n\nAlso need to confirm each kernel's device writes finish before the device-to-host copy, which synchronous default-stream memcpy guarantees, and that each OpenMP thread binds to its device once via cudaSetDevice before the parallel work begins, since CUDA's current-device setting is thread-local.\n\nPerformance-wise, the per-iteration barriers, broadcast, and synchronous copy add small overhead compared to kernel execution time, so the design should scale fine. I'm now sketching the kernel itself: one thread per (row, column) pair, computing updated distances and path entries against the pivot row and column, using local row-indexed storage since each device only holds its assigned rows.\n\nI'm reasoning through whether concurrent reads/writes to the pivot row and column during relaxation cause a race — working out that since distances along the pivot row/column never actually decrease during their own update, no thread ever writes a changed value there, so using the broadcasted pivot row buffer directly for those reads is safe.\n\nThe kernel is memory-bound: each thread reads the pivot row coalesced across j, reads the local pivot column value once, then does the compare-and-write, so there's little left to optimize beyond the existing access pattern.\n\nA fully blocked/tiled Floyd-Warshall would squeeze out more performance, but that adds significant complexity versus the standard per-k broadcast approach with MPI, so I'll just note it as a possible future improvement rather than implement it. I'm also considering pinned host memory for the row transfer buffers to speed up the async copies, but will keep things synchronous for now to avoid correctness pitfalls.\n\nI need to handle the edge case of ranks owning zero rows — they still need to participate in the broadcast and barriers, but should skip allocation and kernel launches when their row count is zero. For the multithreaded part, I'll set the thread count equal to the device count and have each thread compute its own row sub-range, guarding against empty sub-blocks; if no GPUs are available at all, the program should just print an error and exit since GPU usage is mandatory.\n\nFor validation I'll gather the full distance matrix to rank 0 after the computation using MPI_Gatherv with row-based counts and offsets, so rank 0 can print and validate results. As for timing scope, I'm deciding to include both the host-to-device upload and device-to-host download within the timed region, to fairly capture everything needed for the distributed GPU computation rather than just the kernel execution itself.\n\nEach rank redundantly generates the full n×n distance matrix using the original deterministic generator, then extracts its own row block — this is slightly wasteful but simple and cheap. I'm working through how the path matrix initialization assigns successor values symmetrically so that path[i][j] and path[j][i] get set correctly from the nested loop.\n\nI realize that allocating full n×n matrices per rank won't scale well — for large n (like 32768) that's multiple gigabytes per rank just for the distance matrix. For true parallel scalability I should instead generate only each rank's local rows directly rather than materializing the whole matrix everywhere.\n\nFor the rand sequence, since rand_r is inherently sequential, each rank can still walk through the full index sequence but discard results outside its local row range, keeping only what it owns — this costs extra compute per rank but avoids the memory blowup, and should still run in a few seconds even at large n. For the path matrix I'll mirror the original initialization logic but only populate local rows, since path[a][b] always resolves to b regardless of ordering.\n\nFor memory, I'm realizing the path matrix is never actually read in the final output, so full gather of path across ranks may be unnecessary — only dist needs to be fully collected on rank 0 for printing/validation, keeping path device-local or skipped entirely to save memory on large n.\n\nI'm working out argument parsing and output: rank 0 handles all printing and errors, while all ranks call MPI_Init first before parsing. Before I write the new code, here is the design:\n\n- **Equivalence:** In iteration `k`, row `k` and column `k` never change (dist[k][k]=0), so each row `i` can be updated independently with a snapshot of row `k`. Owner of row `k` broadcasts it each iteration.\n- **OpenMP:** One thread per GPU on each node, each driving its own device and sub-block of rows, with double-buffered pivot rows.\n- **CUDA:** A kernel updates each device's rows per pivot. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792974678251,"sessionID":"ses_e8a6413d6ffeN2O07GMBQ08QWq","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01ER4xNvaG5ydZH5jqxYQLaA","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r1/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   MPI    : matrix rows (source nodes) are split into contiguous blocks, one per rank.\n//            For every pivot k, the rank owning row k broadcasts it to all ranks.\n//   OpenMP : within a rank, one thread per visible GPU (node-local share). Each thread\n//            drives its own device and owns a contiguous sub-block of the rank's rows.\n//            Threads synchronize per pivot and share the broadcast pivot row.\n//   CUDA   : each device updates its sub-block of rows for pivot k with one kernel launch.\n//\n// Semantics are identical to the serial algorithm: for a fixed k, row k and column k are\n// invariant (dist[k][k] == 0), so every (i, j) update within a pivot step reads the same\n// values regardless of execution order. The pivot-step loop over k remains sequential.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr unsigned int INF = 1000000000;\nconstexpr unsigned int MAX_DISTANCE = 200;\n\n// Index calculation for flattened 2D array\ninline constexpr size_t idx2(const size_t i, const size_t j, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    return j * n + i;\n}\n\nstatic int gRank = 0;\nstatic int gSize = 1;\n\n[[noreturn]] static void fatal(const char* msg) {\n    fprintf(stderr, \"[rank %d] fatal: %s\\n\", gRank, msg);\n    fflush(stderr);\n    MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    std::abort();\n}\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                       \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                       \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"[rank %d] CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", gRank, __FILE__,     \\\n                    __LINE__, cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                 \\\n            fflush(stderr);                                                              \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Row-block partition of [0, numNodes) over gSize ranks: rank r owns [start[r], start[r+1]).\nstatic std::vector<size_t> makeRowPartition(const size_t numNodes, const int parts) {\n    std::vector<size_t> start(parts + 1);\n    for (int r = 0; r <= parts; ++r) {\n        start[r] = numNodes * static_cast<size_t>(r) / static_cast<size_t>(parts);\n    }\n    return start;\n}\n\n// Generates the same distance values as the serial reference (same RNG stream, same\n// linear order) but only stores the rows [rowBegin, rowEnd) into `local`.\nvoid initializeDistanceRows(std::vector<unsigned int>& local, const size_t numNodes,\n                            const size_t rowBegin, const size_t rowEnd,\n                            const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n    const size_t lo = rowBegin * numNodes;\n    const size_t hi = rowEnd * numNodes;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes * numNodes; ++i) {\n        const unsigned int value =\n            rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n        if (i >= lo && i < hi) {\n            local[i - lo] = value;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = rowBegin; i < rowEnd; ++i) {\n        local[(i - rowBegin) * numNodes + i] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\n// Same values as the serial path initialization, restricted to rows [rowBegin, rowEnd).\nvoid initializePathRows(std::vector<unsigned int>& local, const size_t numNodes,\n                        const size_t rowBegin, const size_t rowEnd) {\n    for (size_t r = rowBegin; r < rowEnd; ++r) {\n        unsigned int* row = local.data() + (r - rowBegin) * numNodes;\n        for (size_t c = 0; c < numNodes; ++c) {\n            row[c] = static_cast<unsigned int>(r);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// One pivot step k for a block of local rows [0, rows):\n//   dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]); path[i][j] = k on improvement.\n// rowK holds the (unchanged during step k) row k of the full matrix.\n__global__ void fwPivotKernel(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path,\n                              const unsigned int* rowK,\n                              const size_t rows, const size_t n, const size_t k) {\n    const size_t j = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (j >= n) {\n        return;\n    }\n    const size_t stride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.y) * blockDim.y;\n    for (size_t li = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y; li < rows;\n         li += stride) {\n        const size_t base = li * n;\n        const unsigned int distIK = dist[base + k];\n        const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n        if (newDist < dist[base + j]) {\n            dist[base + j] = newDist;\n            path[base + j] = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n\n    // 1. Diagonal should be zero\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        if (dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] != 0) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: diagonal element [%zu,%zu] is not zero\\n\", i, i);\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // 2. Triangle inequality: dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] >= dist[i][j]\n    // Check a sample of paths to avoid O(n^3) validation time\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++j) {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n\n                // Check for overflow before addition\n                if (distIK < INF && distKJ < INF) {\n                    if (distIK + distKJ < distIJ) {\n                        printf(\"Validation failed: triangle inequality violated at [%zu,%zu,%zu]\\n\",\n                               i, j, k);\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of nodes in the graph (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nstruct DeviceSlice {\n    int device;\n    size_t begin;  // local row range [begin, end) within this rank's block\n    size_t end;\n};\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = 0;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n    if (provided < MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED) {\n        fatal(\"MPI implementation does not support validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numNodes = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of nodes: %zu\\n\", numNodes);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Node-local rank and GPU assignment\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, gRank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0, localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &localSize);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices));\n    if (numDevices <= 0) {\n        fatal(\"no CUDA devices available\");\n    }\n    const int numThreads = std::max(1, numDevices / localSize);\n    omp_set_dynamic(0);\n\n    // Row partition across ranks and local partition across this rank's threads/devices\n    const std::vector<size_t> rowStart = makeRowPartition(numNodes, gSize);\n    const size_t rowBegin = rowStart[gRank];\n    const size_t rowEnd = rowStart[gRank + 1];\n    const size_t localRows = rowEnd - rowBegin;\n\n    std::vector<DeviceSlice> slices(numThreads);\n    for (int t = 0; t < numThreads; ++t) {\n        slices[t].device = (localRank * numThreads + t) % numDevices;\n        slices[t].begin = localRows * t / numThreads;\n        slices[t].end = localRows * (t + 1) / numThreads;\n    }\n\n    // Allocate and initialize (not timed, as in the original)\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Initializing graph...\\n\");\n    }\n    std::vector<unsigned int> hDist(localRows * numNodes);\n    std::vector<unsigned int> hPath(localRows * numNodes);\n    initializeDistanceRows(hDist, numNodes, rowBegin, rowEnd, 1, MAX_DISTANCE);\n    initializePathRows(hPath, numNodes, rowBegin, rowEnd);\n\n    // Full result matrices exist only on the root, for output and validation\n    std::vector<unsigned int> dist;\n    std::vector<unsigned int> path;\n    if (root) std::vector<unsigned int> rowBuf[2];\n    rowBuf[0].resize(numNodes);\n    rowBuf[1].resize(numNodes);\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Computing shortest paths...\\n\");\n    }\n\n    double 0;\n            while (owner + 1 < gSize && rowStart[owner + 1] <= k) ++owner;\n\n            unsigned int* buf = rowBuf[k & 1].data();\n\n            // The thread holding row k copies it from its device into the host buffer\n            if (owner == gRank && rows > 0) {\n                const size_t kLocal = k - rowBegin;\n                if (kLocal >= s.begin && kLocal < s.end) {\n cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n                }\n            }\n#pragma omp barrier\n#pragma omp master\n            {\n                MPI_Bcast(buf, static_cast<int>(numNodes), MPI_UNSIGNED, owner, {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792974916714,"sessionID":"ses_e8a6413d6ffeN2O07GMBQ08QWq","part":{"id":"prt_175a1f1b5001s5TZ3c6WlgkBu3","messageID":"msg_175a1ee00001bBs4Lml95EooBa","sessionID":"ses_e8a6413d6ffeN2O07GMBQ08QWq","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm seeing solid speedups (~45x at 2048) with 2 ranks, but 3 ranks performs worse despite each rank having its own GPU on the same node—likely because per-iteration synchronization overhead grows disproportionately with 3 ranks.\n\nLooking at the single-GPU kernel numbers for 2048, the throughput is clearly memory-bound—around 660GB/s of traffic for a 207ms run, matching the memory bandwidth ceiling rather than compute limits. A blocked/tiled Floyd-Warshall could substantially speed this up by keeping pivot rows in shared memory, and I'm confident this restructuring preserves exact path correctness since the algorithm's k-ordering semantics remain intact within blocks.\n\nGiven the effort tradeoff, I think I'll leave the current approach as-is and just note this as a known limitation rather than attempting the full blocked rewrite with MPI distribution. I should still sanity-check correctness for edge cases like more ranks than matrix rows—testing np=9 with n=5 where several ranks end up with zero rows assigned.\n\n","time":{"start":1792974909877,"end":1792974916654},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
